claims.text: Role in MG: pyridostigmine PO, titrated to Sx; neostigmine if parenteral tx is needed (eg, dysphagia);
claims.quote: Pyridostigmine is administered orally, with dose titrated based on symptoms. When parenteral therapy is necessary (eg, because of dysphagia), neostigmine may be substituted.

claims.text: abdominal cramps and diarrhea → oral atropine or propantheline.
claims.quote: Anticholinesterase medications can cause abdominal cramps and diarrhea, which are treated with oral atropine or propantheline.

claims.text: Cholinergic crisis: weakness from too high an anticholinesterase dose; mild crisis can mimic worse MG;
claims.quote: Cholinergic crisis is muscular weakness that can result when the dose of anticholinesterase medications (eg, neostigmine, pyridostigmine) is too high. A mild crisis may be difficult to differentiate from worsening myasthenia.

claims.text: severe crisis: fasciculations, ↑lacrimation and salivation, tachy, diarrhea.
claims.quote: Severe cholinergic crisis can usually be differentiated because, unlike myasthenia gravis, it results in muscle fasciculations, increased lacrimation and salivation, tachycardia, and diarrhea.

claims.text: Pyridostigmine bromide (Mestinon) dose, myasthenia gravis: Avg dose ten 60 mg tablets or ten 5 mL teaspoonfuls daily, spaced for max relief when needed.
claims.quote: The average dose is ten 60 mg tablets or ten 5 mL teaspoonfuls daily, spaced to provide maximum relief when maximum strength is needed.

claims.text: Severe cases: up to 25 tablets/teaspoonfuls a day; mild: one to six daily.
claims.quote: In severe cases as many as 25 tablets or teaspoonfuls a day may be required, while in mild cases one to six tablets or teaspoonfuls a day may suffice.

claims.text: TIMESPAN 180 mg: one to three tablets once or twice daily; ≥6 h between doses.
claims.quote: One to three 180 mg tablets, once or twice daily, will usually be sufficient to control symptoms; however, the needs of certain individuals may vary markedly from this average. The interval between doses should be at least 6 hours.

claims.text: Pyridostigmine bromide (Mestinon) CI and cautions: CI: mechanical intestinal or urinary obstruction.
claims.quote: MESTINON is contraindicated in mechanical intestinal or urinary obstruction

claims.text: Use w particular caution in bronchial asthma.
claims.quote: particular caution should be used in its administration to patients with bronchial asthma

claims.text: Pyridostigmine bromide (Mestinon) cholinergic crisis: Overdosage may cause cholinergic crisis — increasing muscle weakness that may lead to death via respiratory muscle involvement.
claims.quote: As is true of all cholinergic drugs, overdosage of MESTINON may result in cholinergic crisis, a state characterized by increasing muscle weakness which, through involvement of the muscles of respiration, may lead to death.

claims.text: Cholinergic crisis tx: prompt withdrawal of all drugs of this type; immediate atropine also recommended.
claims.quote: calls for the prompt withdrawal of all drugs of this type. The immediate use of atropine in cholinergic crisis is also recommended.

claims.text: Atropine may abolish GI/muscarinic side effects, but by masking signs of overdosage can lead to inadvertent cholinergic crisis.
claims.quote: Atropine may also be used to abolish or obtund gastrointestinal side effects or other muscarinic reactions; but such use, by masking signs of overdosage, can lead to inadvertent induction of cholinergic crisis.

claims.text: Pyridostigmine bromide (Mestinon) adverse reactions and renal dosing: SEs mostly related to overdosage: muscarinic (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal cramps, ↑ peristalsis/salivation/bronchial secretions, miosis, diaphoresis) and nicotinic (muscle cramps, fasciculation, weakness).
claims.quote: The side effects of MESTINON are most commonly related to overdosage and generally are of two varieties, muscarinic and nicotinic. Among those in the former group are nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal cramps, increased peristalsis, increased salivation, increased bronchial secretions, miosis and diaphoresis. Nicotinic side effects are comprised chiefly of muscle cramps, fasciculation and weakness.

claims.text: Mainly excreted unchanged by kidney — lower doses may be required in renal disease; treatment based on titration of drug dosage to effect.
claims.quote: Pyridostigmine is mainly excreted unchanged by the kidney.6,7,8 Therefore, lower doses may be required in patients with renal disease, and treatment should be based on titration of drug dosage to effect.
